terms.gloss: a noun for something that cannot be seen and touched
evidence: Quint. 1.4.20: appellātiō, cui vel alterum deesset vel utrumque, ventus, caelum, deus, virtūs
terms.comment: Some grammarians, Quintilian reports, divided common nouns into vocābula, things seen and touched (domus, lectus), and appellātiōnēs, things lacking one or both (ventus, virtūs); Quintilian himself thought the division of little use. Traupman takes these as abstract and concrete nouns (245): bonitās, goodness.

phrases.latin: ut esset vocābulum corpus vīsū tāctūque manifestum, domus, lectus, appellātiō, cui vel alterum deesset vel utrumque, ventus, caelum, deus, virtūs
phrases.english: so that a vocābulum was a body plain to sight and touch, a house, a bed, an appellātiō one that lacked either or both, wind, sky, god, virtue

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 245.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
